rationale:
Issue #98 ('Wrapped lines in AnsiTreeView lose their styling') with bug label describes multiline tree values losing ANSI color styling. The minimized production patch replaces plain string substitution with per-line styled buffer writes in the isMultiline branch, preserving theme.valueTheme.textStyle and color on continuation lines. The trigger test 'long text with colors' verifies cadetBlue styling appears on wrapped lines via golden comparison. The patch changes only `final` to mutable for lines variable and replaces the single text.replaceAll line with a loop that applies styling; no refactoring, feature extension, or unrelated changes. Runtime evidence shows buggy revision fails the trigger deterministically (3 fingerprint groups over 3 reps) while fixed passes; full suite confirms no regression. The trigger test originates in the fixing commit but uses pre-existing API (AnsiTreeViewTheme, AnsiTreeNodeValueTheme with wrapText/wrapLength/color fields referenced in parent hunks), making it semantically equivalent to the reported defect. No active duplicates in the same project.

Issue #98 ('Wrapped lines in AnsiTreeView lose their styling', labeled bug) reports that multiline values lose formatting when wrapped. The minimized production patch replaces the old string replaceAll approach (which never styled continuation lines) with explicit per-line iteration that applies theme.valueTheme.textStyle and foregroundColor to every line via writeStyled/styled methods. The trigger test 'long text with colors' validates that multiline values with AnsiColor.cadetBlue are correctly styled across all lines, matching the defect description. The patch changes only the multiline branch logic (final→mutable variable, replaceAll→loop with styling, early return) with no refactoring, documentation, or configuration changes. The trigger test and mock are added in the same commit but use only pre-existing API (AnsiTreeViewTheme, AnsiTreeNodeValueTheme with wrapText/wrapLength/color fields referenced in parent code). Strict validation confirms deterministic differential behavior: buggy version reproduces only this trigger, fixed version passes all tests across 32 matrix runs with 3 repetitions. No active duplicates in the same project.
